resources.name: DH

Unlike RSA, the Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange is not encryption, and is only a way for two parties to agree on a shared secret value. Since the keys generated are completely pseudo-random, DH key exchanges can provide forward secrecy (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_secrecy).

resources.name: MD5

It can still be used as a checksum to verify data integrity, but only against unintentional corruption.

resources.name: SHA1

resources.name: SHA2

They use different shift amounts and additive constants, but their structures are otherwise virtually identical, differing only in the number of rounds.

resources.name: SHA3
resources.desc: Cryptographic hash function that produces a fixed-size output, typically 224, 256, 384, or 512 bits, from variable-size input data. It is part of the SHA-3 family of cryptographic algorithms designed to resist attacks from quantum computers and offers security properties such as pre-image resistance, second pre-image resistance, and collision resistance.
